newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Supported by demand, draw in stocks.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Supported by demand, draw in stocks.

text.p: Anticipation for healthy demand from a local trader coupled with the low level of Singapore residue stocks supported the high sulphur fuel oil market on Thursday, traders said.
Bids and offers for the 180-cst grade were active with prices moving within a recent narrow range of $100-$102 per tonne but no deal was heard.
Fresh Chinese enquiries boosted sentiment and several fuel oil tenders from India and South Korea also supported prices, traders said.
A Chinese trader was heard bidding for 15,000 tonnes of 380-cst grade, 3.5-percent fuel oil to South China with at $8.00-per-tonne above Singapore's published quotes on a c-and-f basis.
Another bid for 15,000 tonnes of 380-cst grade, 0.5 percent was heard at $13-per-tonne also above Singapore published quotes.
Some traders were bullish on a recent price rise, citing a drop in Singapore's weekly residue stocks and the current regional turnaround season.
Singapore weekly residue stocks fell by 1.096 million barrels to 10.664 milllion barrels in the week ending March 26, the Trade Development Board (TDB) said.
"The residue stocks are low now and South Korea has entered the turnaround season which should extend into April and May," said one trader.
"Demand should be quite healthy in the near term," he said.
However, most traders agreed that current supplies remained sufficient and some unsold cargoes could limit the upward sentiment.
